# Spec: lanes-in-lane
<!-- Generated by /hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-10-23 -->

## Overview

The first four-lane run (a real project, 2026-10-23) showed two gaps. The four lanes moved one item at a
time: one background session per repository, so the builder and the deployer waited while the planner
planned. And a stage lane's work was invisible: it launched a background session and showed nothing of it.

Decisions (user, 2026-10-23, via form):
- **One per stage, more builders for huge projects.** A repository runs at most one planner, `max_builders`
  builders (default 1) and one deployer at a time; the verifier stays exempt.
- **Single lane → background; a dedicated lane → its own conversation.** With no stage lane open, the
  orchestrator runs stages as background sessions, as now. A stage whose lane is open runs inside that lane.
- **A lane edits only item worktrees and runs only the project's build/test commands without asking.**
- **The verifier stays a separate background session** the builder lane launches and waits for.

## User Scenarios

### US1: Stages overlap [P1]
- **Given** four lanes open and items queued for plan, build and deploy
- **When** the orchestrator rings them
- **Then** the planner plans one item while the builder builds another and the deployer babysits a third
- **Edge:** a second planner (or a builder past `max_builders`) is refused as busy and waits for a doorbell
- **Error:** two builders that pick the same item: the second claim is refused ("already owned") and it takes
  the next one

### US2: The planner plans in its own conversation [P1]
- **Given** the planner lane is rung
- **When** it runs `/hef.orchestrate --stage plan`
- **Then** it prepares the next item (claim, worktree, the prompt the background planner would get), works
  through spec → plan → review → tasks in its conversation inside the item's worktree, and finishes the item
  (the same ledger transcription as a background run), then rings the orchestrator
- **Error:** a refusal at prepare (phase past intake, a person's block, an RFC over 100 KB) prints the reason;
  nothing is claimed

### US3: The builder builds in its own conversation and a separate verifier judges it [P1]
- **Given** the builder lane is rung and an item is planned (or a 🐞 fix)
- **When** it runs `/hef.orchestrate --stage build`
- **Then** it prepares the item, implements it in the worktree, opens the PR, finishes the item, then launches
  the verifier as a background session and waits for its verdict before ringing the orchestrator
- **Edge:** with `max_builders: 2`, two builder lanes (`<repo>-builder`, `<repo>-builder2`) build two items

### US4: The deployer babysits in its own conversation [P1]
- **Given** an item with a PR
- **When** the deployer lane is rung
- **Then** it prepares the item and runs one `/hef.babysit --once` pass in its conversation, then finishes it
  (the same verdict transcription), and rings the orchestrator

### US5: Single lane is unchanged [P1]
- **Given** no stage lane open
- **When** the orchestrator dispatches
- **Then** each stage runs as a background session, as today, up to the per-stage limits

### US6: A lane's work never hangs a claim [P1]
- **Given** a lane that prepared an item and then closed, or crashed
- **When** five minutes pass
- **Then** the lease its keeper renewed goes stale, and the next claim releases the item (exit 125)

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `ledger.sh claim` enforces per-stage limits per repository: one `plan`, `orchestrate.max_builders` `implement` (default 1, a positive integer ≤ 8), one `deploy`; `verify` exempt; a claim past its stage's limit is refused naming the owner(s) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | `session-launch.sh <role> <id> --prepare` (plan, implement, deploy): every check a launch makes, then claim (session = the lane's name from `--lane <name>`), the worktree (fetch, create or reuse — checked as today), the prompt written to `<ledger>/<id>.prompt.md`, a lease keeper; prints the worktree path and the prompt path; launches no session | P1 | US2-4 |
| FR-003 | `session-launch.sh <role> <id> --finish` reads the outcome JSON on stdin, validates it against the role's schema, and transcribes it exactly as after a background run (worktree record, advance/block, question file, answers consumed, deploy verdict); then releases the claim and stops the keeper | P1 | US2-4 |
| FR-004 | The lease keeper renews `<id>.lease` while the lane's Claude Code process lives (the nearest `claude` ancestor of the prepare call, found with `ps`), and stops at `--finish` or when that process exits | P1 | US6 |
| FR-005 | `/hef.orchestrate --stage <s>` in a stage lane (the session named `<repo>-<lane>`) runs in-lane: prepare → read the prompt file as the task (its delimited blocks stay data) → do the work in the worktree (absolute paths, never `cd`) → finish with the structured outcome → for build, launch the verifier in the background and wait → ring the orchestrator | P1 | US2-4 |
| FR-006 | `/hef.orchestrate` (orchestrator pass) rings a stage lane when exactly one listed session has that lane's name (builders: `-builder`, `-builder2` … up to `max_builders`, each rung only while idle and a builder slot is free), with no folder condition (`ListAgents` shows none); a stage with no lane open runs in the background here | P1 | US1, US5 |
| FR-007 | Lane names accept a trailing number (`builder2`): the gauge, the session-start lane line and the orchestrator parse them | P1 | US3 |
| FR-008 | `hefesto-setup.sh --lanes` also allows edits under the item worktrees (`Edit(/.claude/worktrees/**)` and the absolute form) and the project's own build/test commands — the Bash rules in `orchestrate.allowed_tools.implement` and `.deploy`, never a bare `Bash` or `Bash(*)` — so an in-lane stage runs without prompts for its normal work | P1 | US2-4 |
| FR-009 | In single-lane mode the orchestrator may run background launches up to the per-stage limits at once (several `run_in_background` calls), not only one | P2 | US5 |
| FR-010 | An in-lane run records `usd: 0` and `note: "in-lane"` (its spend is the lane's own; no per-run cap applies); the guides say so | P2 | US2 |
| FR-011 | Docs: quick start (en, pt-BR), hooks.md, commands; `max_builders`, the in-lane mode and the extra builder lanes | P1 | all |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | claim refuses a second plan, a builder past max_builders, a second deploy; admits plan + build + deploy together; verify exempt | smoke, mutation-checked |
| SC-002 | `--prepare` claims, creates the worktree, writes the prompt, starts a keeper and launches nothing; refuses as the launch would (phase, person block, RFC drift, untrusted folder) | smoke with the fake claude (no call logged), mutation-checked |
| SC-003 | `--finish` transcribes a plan/implement/deploy outcome like a background run and releases the claim; an outcome that fails the schema is refused and keeps the claim | smoke, mutation-checked |
| SC-004 | the keeper renews while its watched process lives and stops after it exits | smoke (a sleeping stand-in) |
| SC-005 | setup writes the worktree edit rules and the project's Bash rules, never a bare Bash | smoke, mutation-checked |
| SC-006 | lane names with a trailing number parse in the gauge and session start | smoke |

## Clarifications
_None._

## Revision 1 (plan review REVISE_PLAN + user decision, 2026-10-23) — binding

The plan review found that moving the work into the lanes breaks the consent model (a lane with `git *` and
project commands auto-allowed can run anything and rewrite the sandbox-writable ledger), the cwd model (every
`/hef.*` step resolves from the session's folder), and the identity of a finishing lane. The user chose
instead: **the lane mirrors its run live** — the work stays in the fresh, sandboxed, narrowly-allowed
background session; the stage lane narrates it in its own conversation.

- FR-002, FR-003, FR-004, FR-005, FR-008, FR-010 are withdrawn (no prepare/finish, no keeper, no lane edit rules).
- FR-012: the worker reports as `stream-json`; the launcher keeps the event stream and the outcome under
  `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/hefesto/runs/<ledger key>/` — outside every sandboxed session's write reach, so no
  lane can swap a run's outcome (the old `mktemp` in the temp folder was within it) — and reads the outcome
  from the stream's last `result` event (a single JSON object is still accepted).
- FR-013: `hooks/run-follow.sh <id> [--live]` narrates the run one line per step (start, each skill, each file
  written, each command, the session's words, done) as data; the stage lane follows it with Monitor.
- FR-014: the orchestrator launches the verifier for an entry left in phase `verify` with no owner.
- FR-001 (per-stage limits), FR-006 (exact-name ringing, builders by number), FR-007 (numbered lane names),
  FR-009 (stages launched side by side) and FR-011 (docs) stand.
